title: Single-cell ATAC-seq
text:
Course Overview

This course introduces the analysis of single-cell ATAC-seq (scATAC-seq) data in R using the Signac and Seurat packages. scATAC-seq measures chromatin accessibility in thousands of individual cells, letting us map regulatory regions and identify cell types and states from the epigenome rather than the transcriptome.
The course runs as a one-day workshop split into four sessions:








Session
Time
Topic




1
9:30–11:00
Foundations — chromatin accessibility, the costs and benefits of single-cell resolution, Cell Ranger ATAC outputs, fragment files and importing data into Signac/Seurat



11:00–11:15
Break


2
11:15–12:45
QC and Preprocessing — scATAC-specific QC metrics, filtering thresholds, TF-IDF normalization and peak-set selection



12:45–1:45
Lunch


3
1:45–3:15
Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering — LSI, UMAP, graph-based clustering, gene activity scores and label transfer from scRNA-seq



3:15–3:30
Break


4
3:30–4:30
Differential Accessibility and Visualization — marker-based and pseudobulk differential accessibility, and coverage plots of regions of interest



Some familiarity with R and with single-cell RNA-seq analysis in Seurat is assumed.
Course material and exercises are available to view as rendered HTML at https://rockefelleruniversity.github.io/scATAC/. All material is available to download under GPL v2 license.

System Requirements


Install R
R can be installed from the R-project website.
The R website can be found here http://www.r-project.org/. This website has all the latest information about R updates, conferences and installation
You can use this direct links to the install for each major OS:

Mac
Windows

Install RStudio
RStudio can be installed from the RStudio website.
http://www.rstudio.com/
RStudio can be downloaded for all platforms at the link below
https://rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/



Install required R packages
R Packages can be installed from the course package or from CRAN/Bioconductor. Once R and RStudio is installed, you can copy and paste these install commands into lower left pane of RStudio which should be labelled “Console”. If you run into any errors, do this one line at a time.

From the course packageFrom CRAN and Bioconductor


install.packages('BiocManager')
install.packages('remotes')
BiocManager::install('RockefellerUniversity/scATAC')


install.packages('BiocManager')
BiocManager::install('methods')
BiocManager::install('ggplot2')
BiocManager::install('Signac')
BiocManager::install('Seurat')
BiocManager::install('SeuratObject')
BiocManager::install('hdf5r')
BiocManager::install('GenomicRanges')
BiocManager::install('IRanges')
BiocManager::install('AnnotationHub')
BiocManager::install('ensembldb')
BiocManager::install('biovizBase')
BiocManager::install('scDblFinder')
BiocManager::install('SingleCellExperiment')
BiocManager::install('DESeq2')






For an environment matching the one this course was built and tested against, use the Bioconductor Docker image, pinned to the Bioconductor release used at compile time. Docker must be installed; run this in a terminal:
docker run -e PASSWORD=changeme -p 8787:8787 bioconductor/bioconductor_docker:RELEASE_3_23
Then open http://localhost:8787 (username rstudio, password changeme) and install the course in the RStudio console:
install.packages('BiocManager')
BiocManager::install('RockefellerUniversity/scATAC')

title: Single-cell ATAC-seq
text:
The Presentations


Single-cell ATAC-seq, Session 1: Foundations
This session introduces the concepts and data structures behind scATAC-seq.

A refresher on chromatin accessibility and ATAC-seq
The benefits and costs of single-cell resolution
Cell Ranger ATAC (and other preprocessor) outputs: fragment files and the peak-by-cell count matrix
Importing data with Signac/Seurat: the ChromatinAssay, fragments, annotations and motifs




Links to presentations:
The html slide presentation can be found at this link Slide
The single page html presentation can be found at this link Single Page
The code use in the presentations can be found at Code
The notebook used to make the presentations can be found at Notebook




Single-cell ATAC-seq, Session 2: QC and Preprocessing
This session covers quality control and preprocessing specific to scATAC-seq data.

Key scATAC QC metrics: TSS enrichment, nucleosome signal, fraction of reads in peaks (FRiP) and blacklist regions
Choosing sensible filtering thresholds
TF-IDF normalization, and why sparse accessibility data are normalized differently from scRNA-seq
Feature selection: choosing a peak set, re-calling peaks and consensus peak sets




Links to presentations:
The html slide presentation can be found at this link Slide
The single page html presentation can be found at this link Single Page
The code use in the presentations can be found at Code
The notebook used to make the presentations can be found at Notebook




Single-cell ATAC-seq, Session 3: Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering
This session moves from a normalized matrix to annotated clusters of cells.

Latent Semantic Indexing (LSI) for dimensionality reduction, and why the first component is usually skipped
UMAP embedding and graph-based clustering
Revisiting QC in light of clustering: analysis as an iterative cycle
Gene activity scores as a proxy for expression: strengths and limitations
Transferring cell-type labels from a scRNA-seq reference




Links to presentations:
The html slide presentation can be found at this link Slide
The single page html presentation can be found at this link Single Page
The code use in the presentations can be found at Code
The notebook used to make the presentations can be found at Notebook




Single-cell ATAC-seq, Session 4: Differential Accessibility and Visualization
This session identifies and visualizes regions that differ in accessibility between groups of cells.

Differential accessibility with FindMarkers
Pseudobulk approaches to differential accessibility
Visualizing regions of interest with coverage plots
